definitions.explanation: Sleeping deeply and soundly without waking, resulting in a well-rested state.

examples.japanese: {昨夜|ゆうべ}は{熟睡|じゅくすい}できた。
{疲|つか}れていたので、{熟睡|じゅくすい}してしまった。
examples.english: I was so tired that I fell into a deep sleep.

examples.japanese: {静|しず}かな{環境|かんきょう}のおかげで、{久|ひさ}しぶりに{熟睡|じゅくすい}することができた。
examples.english: Thanks to the quiet environment, I was able to sleep soundly for the first time in a while.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used with できる ({熟睡|じゅくすい}できた = I slept well) or する ({熟睡|じゅくすい}した = I slept deeply). Implies a particularly restful, uninterrupted sleep — more than just {寝|ね}る (to sleep) or {眠|ねむ}る (to fall asleep).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {爆睡|ばくすい}: sleeping like a log (more casual, emphasizes sleeping so hard you can't be woken)
- {熟睡|じゅくすい}: deep, quality sleep (more neutral/formal)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {熟睡|じゅくすい}する: to sleep soundly
- {熟睡|じゅくすい}できない: can't sleep deeply
- {熟睡|じゅくすい}できる{環境|かんきょう}: an environment conducive to deep sleep
